args.body:
NORTHGALE SYSTEMS, INC.
BOARD APPROVAL PACKAGE — CORVID ANALYTICS MSA (REV B COUNTER-DRAFT)
Prepared by Harrow & Vane LLP for the Northgale Deal Committee
Date: 21 July 2026 (prepared under supplemental GC instruction of 21 July 2026)

-------------------------------------------------------------------
1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Corvid Analytics LLC transmitted its rev B counter-draft of our MSA client form v2 on 9 July 2026 through its counsel, Dahlgren & Pike LLP. Rev B is the operative counter-draft and wholly supersedes the withdrawn rev A. Eight (8) modifications are proposed. Measured against the 2026 Commercial Contracting Playbook, five (5) of the eight proposed changes require escalation because they breach a playbook standard or fall below an approved fallback floor, and one (1) deletion breaches a non-negotiable carve-out. The aggregate financial exposure at the stated $85,000/month base fee, most significantly in the limitation-of-liability cap, is material and requires the Deal Committee to authorize CLO and, where indicated, joint CLO/CFO approvals before any concession is made to Corvid.

The Deal Committee meeting date has moved from 4 August to 29 July 2026. This consolidated package supersedes the stand-alone escalation memorandum commissioned on 14 July 2026 and is filed under the operative name northgale-corvid-msa-board-approval-package.docx.

-------------------------------------------------------------------
2. FINANCIAL PARAMETERS AND LIMITATION-OF-LIABILITY EXPOSURE
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Stated monthly base fee (MSA §4.1): $85,000.

Limitation-of-liability cap — quantified exposure at $85,000/month (playbook PB-5 drafting note):
  • Standard measurement period (24 months): $85,000 × 24 = $2,040,000
  • Corvid's proposed period (12 months): $85,000 × 12 = $1,020,000
  • Approved fallback floor (18 months): $85,000 × 18 = $1,530,000
  • Difference proposal vs. standard: ($1,020,000 reduction, i.e. a 50% cut in cap) = $1,020,000
  • Difference fallback vs. standard: $510,000 reduction

Accepting Corvid's 12-month measurement period would cap Provider exposure at $1,020,000 — $1,020,000 (50%) below the playbook standard and $510,000 below the approved fallback floor of $1,530,000. This is the single largest quantified exposure item in the package.

Other quantified items:
  • Wind-down (rev B §7.4): 60-day full-fee wind-down at $85,000/month = $170,000 of full-fee compensation (2 months × $85,000), which is entirely out of policy (no full-fee wind-down compensation is permitted).
  • Late interest (rev B §4.3): 1.5%/month vs. the 1.0% standard.
  • Service credits (rev B §11.2): 10% aggregate credit cap vs. the 20% standard and 15% fallback floor.

-------------------------------------------------------------------
3. TERM-BY-TERM COMPARISON: CORVID ASK vs. PLAYBOOK STANDARD & APPROVED FALLBACK
-------------------------------------------------------------------

TERM: Section 2.2 — Renewal periods
  Corvid ask: successive two (2) year renewal periods.
  Playbook PB-1 Standard: automatic renewal in one (1) year periods.
  Playbook PB-1 Approved fallback: NONE — multi-year renewal periods of any length are out of policy.
  Assessment: OUT OF POLICY — escalation required. Counter at one-year renewal; do not concede multi-year renewal without CLO approval.
  Required approver: CLO.

TERM: Section 4.3 — Late interest rate
  Corvid ask: 1.5% per month on late undisputed amounts.
  Playbook PB-4 Standard: late interest never above 1.0% per month.
  Playbook PB-4 Approved fallback: none above 1.0%.
  Assessment: OUT OF POLICY — breaches the never-above-1.0% standard. Counter at 1.0%.
  Required approver: CLO (escalation beyond standard).

TERM: Section 4.4 (NEW) — Suspension of services
  Corvid ask: Provider may suspend Services if any undisputed invoice remains unpaid fifteen (15) days after its due date (no cure notice).
  Playbook PB-4 Standard: suspension-of-services rights are out of policy unless preceded by at least thirty (30) days' written cure notice, and any suspension right of any kind requires CFO sign-off.
  Assessment: OUT OF POLICY — Coli's suspension lacks the required 30-day cure notice. Reject absent a 30-day cure notice provision, and any retained suspension right requires CFO sign-off.
  Required approver: CFO.

TERM: Section 7.2 — Termination for convenience notice
  Corvid ask: ninety (90) days' prior written notice.
  Playbook PB-2 Standard: thirty (30) days' notice.
  Playbook PB-2 Approved fallback: up to forty-five (45) days.
  Assessment: OUT OF POLICY — 90 days exceeds the 45-day escalation ceiling. Counter at 30 days, or at most 45 days, without escalation; above 45 days requires CLO approval.
  Required approver: CLO (for any period above 45 days).

TERM: Section 7.4 (NEW) — Wind-down period
  Corvid ask: upon any termination other than for Provider's uncured material breach, a sixty (60) day wind-down during which Customer pays the full monthly base service fee plus all committed third-party costs.
  Playbook PB-3 Standard: wind-down acceptable only if (i) capped at thirty (30) days and (ii) compensation limited to documented out-of-pocket costs and non-cancelable third-party commitments. Full-fee wind-down compensation is out of policy.
  Assessment: OUT OF POLICY — 60 days exceeds the 30-day cap and full-fee compensation is prohibited. Counter with a 30-day wind-down limited to documented out-of-pocket and non-cancelable third-party costs, and reject the 60-day/full-fee ask.
  Required approver: CLO (escalation for out-of-policy wind-down).

TERM: Section 9.1 — Limitation-of-liability measurement period
  Corvid ask: twelve (12) months.
  Playbook PB-5 Standard: twenty-four (24) months.
  Playbook PB-5 Approved fallback floor: eighteen (18) months; twelve (12) months is below the floor and requires CLO approval.
  Assessment: OUT OF POLICY — below the fallback floor. Counter at 18 months (fallback floor) or hold at 24 months; do not accept 12 months without CLO approval.
  Required approver: CLO.
  Quantified exposure: see Section 2 above.

TERM: Section 9.2 — Deletion of gross negligence/willful misconduct carve-out
  Corvid ask: delete clause (c), subjecting gross negligence and willful misconduct to the §9.1 cap.
  Playbook PB-5 Standard: carve-outs for confidentiality, IP indemnification, and gross negligence/willful misconduct are non-negotiable; deletion of any carve-out requires joint CLO and CFO approval.
  Assessment: OUT OF POLICY — deletion of a non-negotiable carve-out. Reject; restore clause (c).
  Required approver: JOINT CLO and CFO.

TERM: Section 11.2 — Service-credit aggregate cap
  Corvid ask: aggregate monthly credit cap of 10% of the monthly base service fee.
  Playbook PB-6 Standard: 20% of the monthly fee.
  Playbook PB-6 Approved fallback floor: fifteen percent (15%); a 10% cap is out of policy.
  Assessment: OUT OF POLICY — below the 15% fallback floor. Counter at 20% (standard) or at minimum 15% (fallback); do not accept 10%.
  Required approver: CLO (escalation below fallback floor).

Acccepted/No-concession items informed by playbook:
  • IP Indemnification (§8) and confidentiality carve-outs (§9.2(a), (b)) retained — acceptable.
  • Base fee, payment terms (net 30), and uptime standard (99.5%) — retained as standard.

-------------------------------------------------------------------
4. REQUIRED APPROVERS
-------------------------------------------------------------------
The following approvals are required before any out-of-policy concession is made to Corvid:
  • CLO approval — renewal periods (multi-year), late interest above 1.0%, convenience-notice above 45 days, wind-down terms, liability-cap measurement below the 18-month fallback floor, service-credit cap below 15%.
  • CFO sign-off — any suspension-of-services right, however structured.
  • JOINT CLO AND CFO approval — deletion of any §9.2 carve-out (here, gross negligence/willful misconduct).

Approval routing: Deal Committee endorses concession recommendations and the CLO and CFO execute the required approvals within their respective sign-off authority before any revised counter-redline is transmitted to Dahlgren & Pike.

-------------------------------------------------------------------
5. COMMITTEE TIMELINE
-------------------------------------------------------------------
The Deal Committee meeting has been moved up from 4 August 2026 to 29 July 2026.
  • 21 July 2026 — This consolidated board approval package finalized and filed.
  • 29 July 2026 — Deal Committee reviews this package and endorses the recommended positions and fallbacks.
  • 30 July 2026 — Following committee endorsement, the CLO/CFO execute required approvals; the counter-redline cover note (prepared under the unchanged 14 July instruction, corvid-msa-counter-redline-cover-note.docx) is finalized to accompany our counter-turn.
  • On approval — Counter-turn redline transmitted to Corvid / Dahlgren & Pike.

-------------------------------------------------------------------
6. APPROVAL REQUEST
-------------------------------------------------------------------
The Deal Committee is respectfully requested to REVIEW and APPROVE the following recommended negotiation positions for the Corvid MSA rev B counter-draft, and to authorize the CLO and CFO to execute the approvals required by the 2026 Commercial Contracting Playbook:

  (a) Renewal (§2.2): hold at one (1) year renewal periods; reject two-year renewal.
  (b) Late interest (§4.3): hold at 1.0% per month.
  (c) Suspension (§4.4): reject any suspension right unless preceded by at least 30 days' written cure notice; authorize CFO sign-off only on that condition.
  (d) Convenience notice (§7.2): counter at 30 days, maximum 45 days.
  (e) Wind-down (§7.4): counter with a 30-day wind-down limited to documented out-of-pocket and non-cancelable third-party costs; reject the 60-day/full-fee ask.
  (f) Liability cap (§9.1): hold at 24 months, counter no lower than the 18-month approved fallback floor ($1,530,000); reject the 12-month/ $1,020,000 ask absent CLO approval.
  (g) Carve-outs (§9.2): restore clause (c) (gross negligence/willful misconduct) as non-negotiable; any deviation requires joint CLO and CFO approval.
  (h) Service credits (§11.2): hold at 20% aggregate cap, counter no lower than 15%; reject the 10% ask.

PRIORITY APPROVAL REQUEST: The most material single concession is the limitation-of-liability cap. Approval is requested to hold the cap at the 24-month standard ($2,040,000) and to concede no lower than the 18-month approved fallback floor ($1,530,000), with the 12-month proposal rejected.

Subject to committee authorization, Harrow & Vane will finalize the counter-redline cover note (corvid-msa-counter-redline-cover-note.docx) reflecting the above positions for transmission to Corvid.

Respectfully submitted,
Harrow & Vane LLP
Counsel to Northgale Systems, Inc.
